Package hadur2.core.gun

Class GunController

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.gun.GunController
public class GunController extends Object
The duel's gun: owns every opponent's gun views, picks which gun aims, scores the virtual guns, learns from each gun wave as it breaks, and chooses the bullet power.

Where it sits in the tick: HadurCore builds a gun wave at every scan of the enemy and hands broken waves to onWaveBreak(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.util.List<hadur2.core.model.RobotState>); on each duel tick it calls aim(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long) (once the gun is within three ticks of cooling) and, when a real bullet goes out, fireVirtualBullets(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long). It asks calculateBulletPower(double, double, double, int) for the power of the next wave, which the core's power policy may then raise (POW-1, POW-2 live there). The opening book's and the tick budget's decisions come in through setOpening(hadur2.core.gun.GunController.Opening) and setKShare(double), and the opponent profile's seeds through seed(java.lang.String, double[], hadur2.core.model.SeedWeight).

Which gun aims, in a duel:

  1. With an opening from the profile, that gun from the first wave (ADAPT-1), until the live virtual-gun ratings differ by more than their margin of error (DIAL-1).
  2. Otherwise head-on until the main view holds DATA_THRESHOLD points that still count, then the anti-surfer gun while its virtual rating is strictly higher, else the main gun (1.20's rule).

With several opponents at the battle's start only the main gun aims and no virtual guns are scored.

Growth is bounded (RES-2): views are per opponent name and each is capped by its tree; the virtual bullets are keyed by wave and cleared at each round's start. Angles are Robocode bearings in radians (0 north, clockwise); guess factors are in [-1, 1].

    • setOpening

      public void setOpening(GunController.Opening opening)
      ADAPT-1: the gun to use from the first firing wave, until the live virtual-gun ratings disagree by more than their margin of error. Null (the default) keeps 1.20's choice: head-on for the first nine waves, then whichever virtual gun rates higher.

      The core sets it from the opening book at the first scan, and back to null once the gun seed is distrusted (RES-4).

      Parameters:
      opening - the opening gun, or null for 1.20's rule

    • seed

      public void seed(String botName, double[] sample, SeedWeight weight)
      ADAPT-3: adds a seeded sample (as the sample sink produced it) to every gun view for botName. The main view takes all ten values, the anti-surfer views the first nine.
      Parameters:
      botName - the opponent
      sample - SAMPLE_WIDTH values: ten features, the guess factor, then the displacement vector's x and y
      weight - the weight every gun seed shares, which the seed trust may lower (RES-4)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the sample is not SAMPLE_WIDTH long

    • liveVerdict

      GunController.Opening liveVerdict(String botName)
      DIAL-1: the gun the live virtual ratings pick, or null while the gap between them is within the margin of error of the better one (Agresti-Coull, 95%).

      The margin used is the larger of the two guns' margins, so either gun's uncertainty holds the opening in place. Null too before the first virtual bullet has been scored.

    • margin

      static double margin(double hits, double n)
      The 95% margin of error of a rate of hits in n (Agresti-Coull).

      Agresti-Coull adds z^2 / 2 (about 2) successes and z^2 (about 4) trials, with z = 1.96, before taking the normal approximation's half-width z * sqrt(p (1 - p) / n). The adjustment keeps the margin sensible at small n and at rates near 0, where the plain formula gives a margin of zero.

    • fireVirtualBullets

      public void fireVirtualBullets(Wave w, Point2D.Double myNextLocation, long currentTime)
      Fires one virtual bullet for each gun along with a real bullet: records the angle each gun would have fired on w, to be scored when the wave breaks. Duels only. The core skips this call at its lowest computation level (TIME-1, TIME-2).
      Parameters:
      w - the wave the real bullet rides
      myNextLocation - where we will be when the bullet leaves
      currentTime - the present tick

    • virtualGunScores

      public double[] virtualGunScores(String botName)
      The virtual guns' battle totals against botName: main-gun waves, main weighted hits, anti-surfer waves, anti-surfer weighted hits. Zeros before any virtual bullet.

      The core folds them into the profile (MEM-2), where they set the movement tier the next opening reads, and checks the gun seed against the main gun's live rating (RES-4).

      Parameters:
      botName - the opponent
      Returns:
      four totals, as above
